I've written the findings file. Three of the four scenarios hold and one has a problem: its test would pass even without the change. I judged everything by reading the code and tests; I ran no tests.

**The problem: "A change moves ownership to a new capability"** (`passes_without_change`)
- Before this change, `change_link_gates` ignored the change's ownership edits and used only the existing ownership rules.
- In the fixture, those rules have `keep` owning both `crates/keep/**` and `crates/split/**`, so the only file nobody owns is `crates/fresh/src/lib.rs`.
- That is exactly the one finding the test expects. So `a_change_moves_ownership_to_a_new_capability` would pass on the old code, and it doesn't show that ownership actually moved to `split`.

**The scenarios that hold:**
- **"Findings of the link gates ownership fixture"**: `link_gates` keeps the existing ownership rules. Nothing owns `crates/fresh/src/lib.rs`, so it gives the expected single `owned-once` finding, and the test checks the rule, node, location, display and fix.
- **"A new capability's ownership overlaps a living one"**: the `fresh` delta's ownership is merged in and the capabilities are sorted by name, which produces `owned by fresh, keep` with the right fix. On the old code this test would fail, because it would report `crates/fresh/src/lib.rs` as unowned instead.
- **"Repository passes the link gates"**: the corpus test no longer filters out any rule, so it fails on any finding, `owned-once` included. It runs `change_link_gates` when `OSQ_CHANGE` is set and not empty, and `link_gates` otherwise. It's marked `#[ignore]`, so it only runs when ignored tests are included, presumably by `scripts/verify-rust.sh`.
